turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come through, have a seat, both of you. I'm Doctor Naidoo. What can I do for you today?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Shame, doctor, it's burning when I pass water again. Third time this year... well, actually, maybe the fourth. I lose track. I nearly stayed at the shop, we've been hectic with the sale.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Burning when you wee, and we'll call it maybe the fourth time this year, not the third. When did this bout start?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Um. A few days ago? Or last week, around my cousin's braai. The robot was out with load shedding, the meat was late, the whole evening was a mess. I can't pin the day, honestly.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She was up and down to the loo all Sunday night. I heard her through the wall.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, I'm running to the toilet the whole time. When I have to go I have to go, I can't hold it. And it's sore low down in my tummy, a dull ache.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is there any blood in the urine?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No blood. It just stings, eina, quite bad, every single time I wee.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does the urine look cloudy, or smell strange?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, it smells a bit strong, sort of off. Not cloudy, not that I've seen. I don't really look, shame.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever, chills, or pain in the back over the kidneys?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, and my back is fine. The flat was baking because the fan died in load shedding, but that's not me being sick.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you vomited?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I haven't vomited. I did feel queasy from those pills, but I didn't bring anything up.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tell me about those pills.

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, don't be cross. I swallowed my sister's leftover antibiotic, the big pink capsules from the bathroom cupboard, and I thought they were two hundred and fifty milligrams, one in the morning and one at night. I took them for three days... no, four days, and I stopped yesterday.

[SEG0017] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Those pink ones are my Ciprobay, ciprofloxacin, and they're five hundred milligrams, not two-fifty. The little white bottle beside them is my biotin, for my hair. Don't mix them up.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): I didn't take the biotin, shame, only the pink capsules. My stomach was turning on them. The queasiness has settled since I stopped yesterday.

[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): So you took her ciprofloxacin twice a day for four days and stopped yesterday. She says five hundred milligrams, you thought two hundred and fifty, and that isn't settled. I won't put a dose down. Did it help the burning at all?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): A little, then it came straight back. For the sting I took Panado, two... actually three, three Panados this morning.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Three Panado this morning. Anything you take every day?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm on the pill, Yaz, one tablet by mouth every night, for contraception. I take it properly.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She does. I take metformin for my sugar, my type two diabetes. That's mine, not hers. She doesn't touch it.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thank you. The metformin and the biotin stay off her list. Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing. No allergies.
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mom always said you got a rash from penicillin when you were small. The clinic wasn't allowed to give it to you.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't remember a rash. I've had Amoxil more than once and I was completely fine. I really don't think I'm allergic to anything.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll mark penicillin as disputed, not confirmed, and I won't use it today. Any vaginal discharge, or itching down below?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. It's just the burning when I wee. It's embarrassing enough with her sitting right here.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): She can wait outside if you'd rather talk alone.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No, it's okay, she drove me. The bakkie's been making a funny noise and she didn't want me in a taxi.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. I can't even stand the smell of it at a braai.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any alcohol?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): A cider now and then. I had one at that braai. I'm not a drinker.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): And work, and who you live with?

[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): I sell clothes at a shop in Musgrave, on my feet the whole day. I live with her in a flat in Glenwood. It's nice, except load shedding kills the wifi and then my series won't play.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any pain in the side? Any chance you could be pregnant?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Side is fine. No, I'm not pregnant. I'm on the pill, the test last month was negative, and my period was two weeks ago, normal.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): How much are you drinking, water-wise?

[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Coffee, mostly. Like four cups at the shop, and then I forget the water. My colleague keeps a Coke for me in the fridge, but it's warm when the power's out and I won't drink it like that.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Coffee can niggle the bladder, so we'll get the water up. Lie back for me, I want to feel your tummy.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Abdomen is soft, no guarding. There's mild tenderness just above the pubic bone. Kidney angles are not tender, either side.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure is one twenty-two over seventy-eight. Pulse is eighty-eight. Temperature is thirty-six point nine. That's reassuring, no fever there.

[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me read this back. Burning every time you pass urine, strong-smelling but not cloudy, with frequency, urgency and a dull low tummy ache, maybe the fourth time this year, and you can't date the start. You took your sister's ciprofloxacin for four days and stopped yesterday, dose not agreed, queasiness settled, three Panado this morning, Yaz every night. No blood, no fever, no vomiting, no loin pain, not pregnant, and you said no vaginal itch or discharge.

[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Well... actually, don't leave it like that. There has been a bit of an itch and a little whitish discharge, not a lot, for a few days along with this. I just didn't want to say it in front of her.
[SEG0047] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I knew it. You've been buying those wipes at Checkers.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, stop, please. It's mild. I'm embarrassed, that's all.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, I'm correcting that. There is mild vaginal itching and a small whitish discharge, current, whatever was said a minute ago. Thank you.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. Sorry. That's the truth of it.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any smell to the discharge? And was sex painful?

[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): No smell that I've noticed. Sex at the weekend was uncomfortable, but I think that was just the burning. My boyfriend reckons I'm being dramatic, he still wants to braai on Saturday.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest, breathing, headaches, bowels?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Chest is fine, no cough, breathing is normal. No headaches. Bowels are normal, I'm not constipated or anything.

[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): My working impression is a lower urine infection, cystitis, from the burning, the frequency and that tenderness. With the itch and the whitish discharge I can't rule out thrush as well, or both together. Nothing is confirmed until we test.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Thrush, shame. I had that once, years ago, after an antibiotic. Is that what the pink capsules did?
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): They can, yes. I'm not starting another antibiotic today, not after the leftover ciprofloxacin, and not while the penicillin question is open.
[SEG0058] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So you'll do a urine test?
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. I'll order a urine dipstick now, and we'll send a sample for microscopy, culture and sensitivities. Please don't take any more of those pink capsules.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, I won't. There's only two left anyway. What if this keeps coming back? And can I work tomorrow? My manager will moan if I miss the sale.

[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the infections keep recurring after this, we might arrange a kidney ultrasound later, not today. Drink plenty of water, don't use leftover antibiotics, wipe from front to back, and you can work if you feel up to it, just don't hold the urine in. If you get a fever, start vomiting, or get pain in the loin, come straight back, don't wait.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. Do I come back otherwise, or only if I'm worse?
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back on Friday for the results either way. If the culture needs a particular antibiotic, I'll prescribe it then.
[SEG0064] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll bring her in the bakkie. And my metformin and my biotin are going in my own bag, not that cupboard.

spec.situation: Woman with burning urine again; says 'third time this year' then corrects to 'maybe the fourth'; took leftover antibiotic from a sister; embarrassed; vaginal symptoms denied, then partly admitted. Urine test ordered.
features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.

bad.reason: Transcript says sister herself has type 2 diabetes, not family history of patient.
Body site urethra not stated; onset uncertainty and burning every time are supported.
bad.text: burning when passing urine (category=genitourinary, status=present, severity=quite bad, frequency=every time she passes urine, onset=unclear, a few days ago or last week, temporality=current, body_site=urethra, reported_by=patient, certainty=uncertain)
